history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed: this is a Sikh gurdwara. The District Sangrur portal lists it as a historic site on the outskirts of Sangrur city marking the place visited by Guru Nanak Dev Ji, Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji, and Guru Tegh Bahadur Sahib Ji. Local tradition (visitor reviews) says Guru Hargobind tied his horse to a Karir tree here, and that a Karir tree regrew through the roof of a room built over its stump - flag as unverified local lore. The gurdwara has a sarovar inside and serves langar; it draws a heavy Sunday rush. Do NOT confuse this with Nankana Sahib (Gurdwara Janam Asthan) in Pakistan's Punjab province, the birthplace of Guru Nanak. Opening hours and founding dates are not published in the consulted sources (flagged verify).

name: Gurudwara Nankiana Sahib
town_description: Sangrur is the district headquarters town in the Malwa region of Punjab, about 69 km from Ludhiana. A former princely-state town (capital of Jind State until 1948), it is the seat of the district administration and the nearest rail and bus hub for surrounding towns.

travel.airport: Ludhiana Airport, about 69 km; Chandigarh Airport, about 107 km (sangrur.nic.in).
travel.railway: Sangrur railway station - town is well connected by rail (sangrur.nic.in).
travel.road: Regular buses from major Punjab cities; on the outskirts of Sangrur city, about 2 km from the town centre (visitor reviews).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant Punjab winter); Baisakhi in April is the main fair time (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published (verify); gurdwaras are generally open to visitors through the day.
